name: ICM | Export People CSV
fixtures: None. Read-only: it fetches Payee and Currency and writes a FILE to workflow storage. It creates and deletes no records, so it is safe to re-run.
note: The anti-drift case is the one that matters here. The search filter is COPIED GROOVY from ICM | Manage People LIST, not a shared node, so the only thing keeping the file equal to the table is a test that asserts both answer the same count for the same search.

cases.name: EXPORT: all-empty-strings is the whole roster
EXPORT: a caller that omits both keys entirely
cases.note: An unbound parameter is a MISSING Groovy variable. Without binding.hasVariable this dies with `No such property: search`.

cases.name: TRUNCATED: a short file says so, and is still a real file
cases.note: maxRows is a runaway guard, not a page size. `matched` comes from includeTotalCount and is NOT capped by the fetch limit, which is what makes a short file impossible to miss.

cases.name: INVALID: non-numeric maxRows is refused BEFORE any fetch
EXPORT: a search matching nothing still writes a header-only file
cases.note: An empty roster is a valid answer, not an error. The file is written deliberately so the reader gets a file with columns rather than a failure.

cases.name: ANTI-DRIFT: the export's search must match Manage People's LIST search
cases.note: If this fails, the two OR-searches have diverged and the Download button no longer returns the rows the table is showing. Compare `matched` here against `total` from the paired case in the Manage People suite.
